lesson.opening: What held the empire together—and which parts survived the western imperial office?

sections.heading: The institutional thread
sections.body:
The principate and provincial administration

Urban life, law, taxation, and the army

Christianity and changing imperial institutions

sections.heading: A model to test
sections.body: Differentiate the western imperial office from Roman law, urban institutions, Christianity, and the eastern empire. Their timelines are not identical.

activities.prompt: “Roman civilization ended everywhere in 476.” — is that an event claim or an interpretation?
activities.hint: This extends a western political event into an unsupported universal conclusion. Track each institution and region separately.

activities.prompt: Put these events back in chronological order.
Describe three institutions that made distant provinces governable.
